subject: botany
question_text: Define root. Mention the types of root systems. Explain how the root is modified to perform different functions.

verification.note: Chapter 5 is sourced from the Junior Fastrack botany book (pp.9-14), which prints the question and a model answer but NO star ranks and NO asked-year citations, so the missing stars/appearances record an absence of signal, not zero frequency. Only ONE source book is held for botany - the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is physics-only and no botany board paper is in the corpus - so the two-book union check and the board-paper back-test are both STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE for this card, not merely pending. The mark split is authored, not printed. BOOK ERRORS RECORDED: the book prints 'radical' for radicle and lists only storage/prop/stilt/assimilatory/nodular in its LAQ answer while its own figure set adds Avicennia pneumatophores, Vanda velamen and Striga; this card includes respiratory and velamen roots per NCERT.

insider_note: Most students write the five modifications but lose the definition mark - start with the radicle line before any list.

steps.label: Root — definition

lines.text: The root is the underground part of the plant

lines: axis. It develops from the radicle of the
germinating seed.
It fixes the plant in the soil and absorbs
water and minerals.
steps.why: The examiner looks for two things in the definition: where the root comes from (the radicle) and what it normally does (fixation and absorption). The book prints 'radical' - the correct word is radicle.
common_mistakes: Writing that the root comes from the plumule. The plumule gives the shoot.
Calling every underground part a root. A rhizome and a corm are underground STEMS.
steps.memory_tip: Radicle gives Root; Plumule gives the shoot. R goes with R.
steps.margin_note: Two lines are enough: origin from the radicle, plus fixation and absorption.

steps.label: Two root systems
lines: Tap root system: in dicots the radicle grows
into the primary root; the primary root and
its branches form the tap root system.
Ex: mustard.
Fibrous root system: in monocots the radicle
is short-lived; a cluster of roots from the
base of the stem forms the fibrous root
system. Ex: paddy.
steps.why: The two systems differ in one fact: whether the radicle survives. In dicots it grows into the tap root; in monocots it dies and roots from the stem base take over.
common_mistakes: Swapping the examples: tap root belongs to dicots, fibrous to monocots.
Forgetting to say the fibrous roots come from the BASE of the stem.
steps.memory_tip: Dicot - Deep tap root. Monocot - Many fibrous roots.
steps.margin_note: Name both systems, one plant group and one example each.

steps.label: Modifications for support
lines: 1. Prop roots: aerial adventitious roots grow
down from horizontal branches, reach the soil
and support the tree like pillars.
Ex: banyan tree.
2. Stilt roots: oblique supporting roots that
develop from the lower nodes of the stem.
Ex: maize, sugarcane.
steps.why: Both are supporting roots; the difference the examiner marks is the origin - prop roots come DOWN from branches, stilt roots come OUT from the lower nodes of the stem.
common_mistakes: Writing banyan for stilt roots and maize for prop roots. It is the reverse.
Calling prop roots tap roots. They are adventitious - they do not come from the radicle.
steps.memory_tip: Prop roots drop from a branch (banyan); stilt roots tilt out from the stem base (maize).
steps.margin_note: One line of function plus one example carries each modification.

steps.label: Storage and respiratory roots
lines: 3. Storage roots: roots become swollen and
tuberous with stored food.
Swollen tap roots: carrot, radish, turnip.
Swollen adventitious roots (fasciculated):
Asparagus.
4. Respiratory roots (pneumatophores): in
mangrove plants the roots grow vertically up,
out of the marshy soil, and take in air.
Ex: Avicennia, Rhizophora.
steps.why: Storage roots change shape (swollen); respiratory roots change direction (they grow up, against gravity, because marshy soil has no air). Naming the habitat - mangroves in marshy soil - is what justifies the upward growth.
common_mistakes: Writing that pneumatophores absorb water. They exchange air; the soil water is all around them.
Listing potato under storage roots. Potato is a stem tuber, not a root.
steps.memory_tip: Carrot, radish, turnip - three swollen tap roots sold in one vegetable shop. Pneumatophores: pneumo = air, as in pneumonia.
steps.margin_note: Give both tap and adventitious storage examples; the examiner looks for pneumatophores by name.

steps.label: Other modifications
lines: 5. Assimilatory roots: green chlorenchymatous
roots that make starch by photosynthesis.
Ex: Taeniophyllum (an epiphyte).
6. Nodular roots: in Fabaceae the roots carry
nodules with the bacterium Rhizobium, which
fixes nitrogen. Ex: groundnut, beans.
7. Velamen roots: epiphytes such as Vanda
absorb moisture from the air through the
spongy velamen tissue.
steps.why: These three show that a root can take over feeding jobs: making food (assimilatory), taking nitrogen (nodular, with Rhizobium) and taking moisture from air (velamen). Naming Rhizobium is the scoring word in nodular roots.
common_mistakes: Writing that Rhizobium harms the plant. It is symbiotic - both partners are helped.
Confusing velamen roots (epiphytes, absorb moisture) with clinging roots (fix the epiphyte to the host).
steps.memory_tip: Feeding jobs in order: food (Taeniophyllum), nitrogen (Rhizobium), moisture (Vanda).
steps.margin_note: In a time squeeze, any two of these with examples still complete the list.

steps.label: Diagram — root modifications
steps.why: One labelled panel per modification is what the examiner can tick: a swollen storage root, prop roots hanging from branches, stilt roots from the lower nodes, and pneumatophores standing above the soil line.
common_mistakes: Drawing pneumatophores below the soil line. Their point is that they come UP out of the soil.
Leaving the panels unlabelled. An unlabelled sketch earns nothing.
steps.memory_tip: Draw the soil line first in each panel; every root modification is placed relative to it.
steps.margin_note: Four small labelled sketches, not one detailed drawing. Two minutes at most.
